system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: VISTA-16 NCT01130246 - VISTA-16 Trial: Evaluation of Safety and Efficacy of Short-term A-002 Treatment in Subjects With Acute Coronary Syndrome
Investigational drug: varespladib
Document: Varespladib methyl in cardiovascular disease (journal, published 2010-10-01, source pmid:20809869)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Varespladib methyl in cardiovascular disease

IMPORTANCE OF THE FIELD: The high risk of recurrent cardiovascular events amongst patients with cardiovascular disease receiving evidence-based therapies has prompted investigations into complimentary treatments that may reduce residual risk. Analyses of clinical trials in statin-treated patients demonstrate that elevated lipid levels and an activated systemic inflammatory state are associated with a higher risk of recurrent cardiovascular events. AREAS COVERED IN THIS REVIEW: This article reviews evidence supporting the causal role for secretory phospholipase A(2) (sPLA(2)) in experimental atherosclerosis, the involvement of various sPLA(2) isozymes as mediators of pro-atherogenic lipoprotein remodeling and participants in vascular and systemic inflammatory responses, and the evidence that sPLA(2) inhibition reduces atherosclerosis in experimental models and biomarkers associated with cardiovascular events in coronary heart disease (CHD) patients. WHAT THE READER WILL GAIN: The experimental basis for sPLA(2) inhibition with varespladib methyl as a potential candidate for lowering recurrent cardiovascular events particularly in acute coronary syndrome patients is discussed. TAKE HOME MESSAGE: Varespladib methyl therapy reduces atherogenic lipoprotein concentrations and systemic inflammatory markers in CHD patients. The future role of varespladib methyl in CHD patients awaits the results of ongoing clinical trials.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
